facts.statement: The name Chasmosaurus means 'opening lizard' because of the large openings in its skull frill.
facts.quote: Its given name means 'opening lizard', referring to the large openings (fenestrae) in its frill

facts.statement: Chasmosaurus was a ceratopsid dinosaur that lived in North America during the Late Cretaceous Period.
facts.quote: Chasmosaurus ( ) is a genus of ceratopsid dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous Period in North America

facts.statement: Lawrence Morris Lambe discovered the first Chasmosaurus remains in 1898 at Berry Creek, Alberta.
facts.quote: In 1898, at Berry Creek, Alberta, Lawrence Morris Lambe of the Geological Survey of Canada made the first discovery of Chasmosaurus remains

facts.statement: The holotype of Chasmosaurus is specimen NMC 491, which consists of a parietal bone from a neck frill.
facts.quote: holotype NMC 491, a parietal bone that was part of a neck frill

facts.statement: A paratype specimen, NMC 2245, found by the Sternbergs in 1913, includes a largely complete skeleton with skin impressions.
facts.quote: Lambe now also assigned a paratype, specimen NMC 2245 found by the Sternbergs in 1913 and consisting of a largely complete skeleton, including skin impressions

facts.statement: All excavated specimens of Chasmosaurus have been found in the Dinosaur Park Formation in Alberta, Canada.
facts.quote: All of the excavated specimens of Chasmosaurus were collected at the Dinosaur Park Formation, Dinosaur Provincial Park, Alberta, Canada

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Chasmosaurus is Chasmosaurus belli.
facts.quote: type_species: Chasmosaurus belli

facts.statement: The genus Chasmosaurus was described by Lambe in 1914.
facts.quote: authority: Lambe, 1914

facts.statement: A 2016 analysis suggested that postorbital horn size is too variable to distinguish between different Chasmosaurus species.
facts.quote: A 2016 analysis of Chasmosaurus specimens by James Campbell and colleagues found that postorbital horn size was too variable to be considered a distinguishing trait

facts.statement: Nicholas Longrich named the genus Mojoceratops in 2010 based on fossils previously assigned to Chasmosaurus.
facts.quote: In 2010, Nicholas Longrich named the new genus and species Mojoceratops perifania based on fossils previously considered to belong to Chasmosaurus

facts.statement: Charles Mortram Sternberg described the species Chasmosaurus russelli in 1940 based on specimen NMC 8800.
facts.quote: Charles Mortram Sternberg added Chasmosaurus russelli in 1940, based on specimen NMC 8800 from southwestern Alberta (lower Dinosaur Park Formation)

facts.statement: Studies published in 2026 supported moving the holotype of C. russelli to the distinct genus Cryptarcus.
facts.quote: Further study of the specimen published in 2026 supported this, and it was moved to the distinct genus Cryptarcus

facts.statement: The species Chasmosaurus mariscalensis, described by Thomas Lehman in 1989, has been renamed Agujaceratops.
facts.quote: Thomas Lehman described Chasmosaurus mariscalensis in 1989 from Texas, which has now been renamed Agujaceratops

facts.statement: The species Chasmosaurus recurvicornis is currently considered taxonomically invalid.
facts.quote: In 2000, George Olshevsky renamed Monoclonius recurvicornis Cope 1889 into Chasmosaurus recurvicornis as its fossil material is likely chasmosaurine; this species is currently considered to be taxonomically invalid

facts.statement: Several research teams have questioned the validity of the genus Mojoceratops following its establishment.
facts.quote: Following the original assignment of the holotype and other skulls to Mojoceratops, several teams of researchers published work questioning the validity of this new genus

facts.statement: Researchers argue that features once thought unique to Mojoceratops, such as grooves on the parietal bone, are actually present in other Chasmosaurus specimens.
facts.quote: Campbell and colleagues, in their 2016 analysis of Chasmosaurus specimens, agreed and added that some supposedly unique features, such as grooves on the parietal bone, were actually also present in the holotype of C. russelli and, to various degrees, in other Chasmosaurus specimens

facts.statement: Some researchers consider specimen CMN 2245 to be a transitional form between C. belli and Vagaceratops.
facts.quote: They also noted that CMN 2245, another former C. belli specimen, represents an additional seemingly transitional specimen between C. belli and Vagaceratops

facts.statement: The taxonomic placement of Vagaceratops remains debated until chasmosaurine relationships are better understood.
facts.quote: Consequently, they suggested it should be maintained as a distinct genus from Chasmosaurus, as its placement would probably remain unstable until chasmosaurine relationships are better understood

facts.statement: Chasmosaurus was a medium-sized ceratopsian dinosaur.
facts.quote: Chasmosaurus was a medium-size ceratopsid.

facts.statement: In 2010, G.S. Paul estimated the length of Chasmosaurus belli at 4.8 meters and its weight at two tonnes.
facts.quote: In 2010 G.S. Paul estimated the length of C. belli at 4.8 metres, its weight at two tonnes.

facts.statement: The rear of the Chasmosaurus frill was V-shaped with straight sides.
facts.quote: The rear of the frill is V-shaped and its sides are straight.

facts.statement: The sides of the frill were adorned with six to ten ornamental bumps called epioccipitals attached to the squamosal bone.
facts.quote: The sides were adorned by six to ten ornamental bumps known as epioccipitals, which attached to the squamosal bone.

facts.statement: Three additional epioccipitals formed by the parietal bones adorned the back of the frill.
facts.quote: Three further epioccipitals adorned the back of the frill, formed by the parietal bones.

facts.statement: The frill was pierced by two large openings called parietal fenestrae, which gave the genus its name.
facts.quote: The frill, formed in the center by the parietals, was pierced by two very large openings, after which the genus was named: the parietal fenestrae.

facts.statement: The parietal fenestrae were triangular with one point oriented toward the frill corner, unlike the oval shape of most relatives.
facts.quote: These were not oval in shape, as with most relatives, but triangular, with one point orientated towards the frill corner.

facts.statement: The first three cervical vertebrae were fused into a unit called a syncervical, a trait shared with other neoceratopsians.
facts.quote: The first three cervical vertebrae are fused into a unit known as a syncervical, as in other neoceratopsians.

facts.statement: A specimen preserved eight cervical vertebrae, likely representing a complete neck.
facts.quote: There are five other cervicals preserved in this specimen, for a total of eight, which likely represents a complete neck.

facts.statement: Chasmosaurus belli possessed a synsacrum, a compound unit made of sacral, dorsal, and sometimes caudal vertebrae.
facts.quote: C. belli possessed a synsacrum, a compound unit composed of sacral, dorsal, and sometimes caudal vertebrae, depending on the specimen.

facts.statement: The specimen NMC 2245 recovered by C.M. Sternberg was accompanied by skin impressions.
facts.quote: The Chasmosaurus specimen NMC 2245 recovered by C.M. Sternberg was accompanied by skin impressions.

facts.statement: The larger scales were hexagonal or pentagonal, having five or six sides.
facts.quote: They were hexagonal or pentagonal, thus with five or six sides.

facts.statement: Small, non-overlapping convex scales about one centimeter in diameter surrounded the larger scales.
facts.quote: Small, non-overlapping convex scales of about one centimetre in diameter surrounded the whole.

facts.statement: The rows of large scales gradually decreased in size from top to bottom.
facts.quote: From top to bottom, the large scale rows gradually declined in size.

facts.statement: Chasmosaurus lived during the late Cretaceous period, approximately 76.5 to 75.5 million years ago in the Campanian stage, in what is now North America.
facts.quote: que vivieron a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 76,5 a 75,5 millones de años, en el Campaniense, en lo que hoy es Norteamérica.

facts.statement: Chasmosaurus is a genus of two known species of ceratopsian ceratopsid dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Chasmosaurus (gr. "lagarto abierto") es un género con dos especies conocidas de dinosaurios ceratopsianos ceratópsidos

facts.statement: Chasmosaurus was initially named Protorosaurus, but that name had already been published for another animal.
facts.quote: Inicialmente ser llamado Protorosaurus, pero este nombre había sido publicado previamente para otro animal.

facts.statement: The type species Chasmosaurus belli comes from the middle and upper layers of the Dinosaur Park Formation in Alberta, Canada, while Chasmosaurus russelli comes from the lower layers of the same formation.
facts.quote: Las dos especies son Chasmosaurus belli proviene de las capas media y superior de la formación Dinosaur Park del Parque provincial de los Dinosaurios de Alberta, Canadá, la especie tipo y Chasmosaurus russelli de las capas inferiores de la misma.

facts.statement: In 1915, Lambe assigned Chasmosaurus within Ceratopsia to the subfamily Chasmosaurinae.
facts.quote: Chasmosaurus was in 1915 by Lambe within the Ceratopsia assigned to the Chasmosaurinae.

facts.statement: The genus authority for Chasmosaurus is Lambe, 1914.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Lambe, 1914

facts.statement: The type species authority is Lambe, 1902, originally named Monoclonius belli.
facts.quote: type_species_authority: Lambe, 1902 [Originalmente Monoclonius belli]

facts.statement: Chasmosaurus russelli was described by Sternberg in 1940.
facts.quote: subdivision: Chasmosaurus russelli Sternberg, 1940

facts.statement: The function of the frill and horns is considered problematic by researchers.
facts.quote: The function of the frill and horns is problematic.

facts.statement: It is possible that the frill was used to appear imposing or for thermoregulation.
facts.quote: It is possible that the frill was simply used to appear imposing or conceivably for thermoregulation.

facts.statement: It is difficult to prove sexual dimorphism in Chasmosaurus.
facts.quote: However, it is difficult to prove any sexual dimorphism.

facts.statement: In 1933, Lull suggested that C. kaiseni was the male of C. belli, which had short brow horns in females.
facts.quote: In 1933, Lull suggested that C. kaiseni, which bore long brow horns, was in fact the male of C. belli of which the females would have short ones.

facts.statement: In 1927, C.M. Sternberg concluded that the smaller skeleton NMC 2245 was male and the larger NMC 2280 was female.
facts.quote: In 1927 C.M. Sternberg concluded that of the two skeletons he had mounted in the Canadian Museum of Nature, the smaller one, NMC 2245, was the male and the larger, NMC 2280, the female.

facts.statement: Today, the two skeletons previously thought to be male and female are referred to different species.
facts.quote: However, today the two are referred to different species.

facts.statement: This indicates that Chasmosaurus was not fast-moving, and juveniles did not need to be fast to keep pace with adults.
facts.quote: This indicates that Chasmosaurus was not fast moving, and that juveniles did not need to be fast moving either to keep pace with adults.

facts.statement: The fossil was complete except for missing front limbs that had fallen into a sinkhole before discovery.
facts.quote: The fossil was complete save for its missing front limbs, which had fallen into a sinkhole before the specimen was uncovered.

facts.statement: Further study revealed that juvenile chasmosaurs had a frill narrower in the back and proportionately shorter relative to the skull compared to adults.
facts.quote: Further study of the specimen revealed that juvenile chasmosaurs had a frill that was narrower in the back than that of adults, as well as being proportionately shorter in relation to the skull.

facts.statement: In 2010, G.S. Paul estimated C. belli was 4.8 meters long and weighed 2 tons, while C. russelli was estimated at 4.3 meters long and 1.5 tons.
facts.quote: En 2010 GS Paul estimó la longitud de C. belli en 4,8 metros, su peso en 2 toneladas; C. russelli tendría 4,3 metros de largo y pesaba 1.5 toneladas.

facts.statement: Like all ceratopsids, Chasmosaurus was a quadrupedal herbivore.
facts.quote: Como todos los ceratópsidos, los chasmosaurios eran cuadrúpedos y herbívoros.

facts.statement: Chasmosaurus had a large frill covering its shoulders and neck, used to deter predators and attract mates, consisting of a bony frame with large openings covered in skin.
facts.quote: Tenían una enorme gola que cubría hombros y cuello, esta la utilizaban para disuadir a los depredadores y atraer a su pareja, este volante era un marco óseo con grandes fenestraciones cubiertas de piel.

facts.statement: Chasmosaurus had a small horn on its nose and two horns above its eyes.
facts.quote: Tenía un cuerno pequeño sobre la nariz y dos sobre sus ojos.

facts.statement: Fossilized skin remains revealed the presence of osteoderms on Chasmosaurus.
facts.quote: El descubrimiento de restos de piel fosilizada de chasmosaurio, reveló la presencia de osteodermos en esta.

facts.statement: The osteoderms were arranged in uniformly spaced rows with five or six sides.
facts.quote: Los osteodermos se ubicaban en filas uniformemente espaciadas, con cinco o seis lados.

facts.statement: Chasmosaurus possessed one of the largest skulls known for any terrestrial animal.
facts.quote: Tenía uno de los cráneos más grandes que se conocen en un animal terrestre.

facts.statement: The skull measured about 2 meters in length, constituting nearly one-quarter of the total body length, and was wider at the back than at the front.
facts.quote: El cráneo medía unos 2 metros de longitud y constituía cerca de una cuarta parte de la longitud total de todo el cuerpo siendo más ancho en la parte trasera que en la parte delantera.

facts.statement: The Chasmosaurus frill is described as heart-shaped because its bone structure consists of two large lobes with a central bone.
facts.quote: El volante del Chasmosaurus se ha descrito como con forma de corazón, puesto que su estructura del hueso consiste en dos grandes lóbulos con un hueso central.

facts.statement: In C. belli, the back of the frill is V-shaped with straight sides, whereas in C. russelli it has a shallow U-shape with more convex sides.
facts.quote: El de C. belli, la parte posterior del volante tiene forma de V y sus lados son rectos. Con C. russelli el borde posterior tiene forma de U poco profunda y los lados son más convexos.

facts.statement: The sides of the frill were adorned with six to nine smaller skin ossifications called epoccipitals or osteoderms, which joined the squamosal bone.
facts.quote: Los lados estaban adornados por seis a nueve osificaciones de piel más pequeñas llamadas los epoccipitales u osteodermos, que se unían al hueso escamoso.

facts.statement: The corner of the frill featured two larger osteoderms on the parietal bone.
facts.quote: La esquina del volante presentaba dos osteodermos más grandes en el hueso parietal.

facts.statement: In C. russelli, the outer osteoderm was the largest, while in C. belli it was the inner one.
facts.quote: Con C. russelli el exterior es el más grande, con C. belli el interno.

facts.statement: The parietal bones of the frill were perforated by very large openings, which gave the genus its name, the parietal fenestrae.
facts.quote: Los huesos parietales del volante fueron perforados por aberturas muy grandes, después de lo cual proviene el nombre del género fue, las fenestras parietales.

facts.statement: These openings were not oval like most relatives but triangular, with a point oriented toward the frill corner.
facts.quote: Estos no eran de forma ovalada, como la mayoría de los parientes, sino triangulares, con un punto orientado hacia la esquina del volante.

facts.statement: The frill may have been brightly colored to attract attention, increase its apparent size, or serve as part of courtship display.
facts.quote: El volante se pudo también haber coloreado brillantemente, llamar la atención aumentando su tamaño o como parte de la exhibición en la época del celo.

facts.statement: However, the large frill was very fragile because it was mainly stretched skin between bones, so it could not provide much functional defense.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, el volante que era tan grande, también era muy frágil, puesto que era principalmente piel estirada entre los huesos, no habría podido proporcionar tan mucha defensa funcional.

facts.statement: It is possible the frill was used simply to appear imposing or for thermoregulation.
facts.quote: Es posible que fue utilizado simplemente para aparecer imponente o para termorregulación.

facts.statement: Various fossil findings have produced inconclusive results, with one species named Ch. kaiseni having long frontal horns while Ch. belli had only short ones.
facts.quote: Diversos hallazgos fósiles han producido los resultados poco concluyentes, una especie de Chasmosaurus, se había nombrado Ch. kaiseni, con cuernos largos de la frente, mientras que Ch. belli tenía solamente unos cortos.

facts.statement: Although initially named as distinct species, it now seems possible that the long horns belonged to males and the shorter horns to females.
facts.quote: Aunque éstos fueran nombrados inicialmente como especie distinta, parece posible ahora que los cuernos largos pertenecieron a los machos y a los cuernos más cortos a las hembras.

facts.statement: The Chasmosaurus specimen NMC 2245 recovered by C.M. Sternberg was accompanied by skin impressions.
facts.quote: El espécimen de Chasmosaurus NMC 2245 recuperado por C. M. Sternberg fue acompañado por impresiones de la piel.

facts.statement: The preserved area of the skin, from the right hip region, measures approximately one by 0.5 meters.
facts.quote: El área conservada, desde la región de la cadera derecha, mide aproximadamente uno por 0.5 metros.

facts.statement: The scales were hexagonal or pentagonal, therefore having five or six sides.
facts.quote: Eran hexagonales o pentagonales, por lo tanto, con cinco o seis lados.

facts.statement: Small convex non-overlapping scales about one centimeter in diameter surrounded the larger scales.
facts.quote: Pequeñas escamas convexas no superpuestas de alrededor de un centímetro de diámetro rodeaban el todo.

facts.statement: The largest scales were wrinkled due to straight grooves oriented perpendicularly to their edges.
facts.quote: Las escamas más grandes estaban arrugadas debido a surcos rectos orientados perpendiculares a sus bordes.

facts.statement: From top to bottom, the rows of large scales gradually decreased in size.
facts.quote: De arriba abajo, las filas de grandes escamas declinan gradualmente en tamaño.

facts.statement: Lawrence Lambe descubrió los primeros restos de Chasmosaurus en 1898, que consistían en partes del volante del cuello.
facts.quote: En 1898, Lawrence Lambe de la Estudio Geológico de Canadá hizo el primer descubrimiento de restos de Chasmosaurus, partes del volante del cuello.

facts.statement: Lawrence Lambe estableció el nombre del género Chasmosaurus en febrero de 1914.
facts.quote: Por lo tanto, Lawrence M. Lambe creó el nombre de reemplazo Chasmosaurus en febrero de 1914.

facts.statement: La especie tipo Chasmosaurus belli fue nombrada en honor al coleccionista Walter Bell.
facts.quote: El nombre específico honró al coleccionista Walter Bell.

facts.statement: El paratipo del género, el espécimen NMC 2245, fue encontrado por los Sternberg en 1913 y conserva un esqueleto casi completo con impresiones de piel.
facts.quote: Lambe ahora también asignó un paratipo, el espécimen NMC 2245 encontrado por los Sternbergs en 1913 y que consiste en un esqueleto en gran parte completo, que incluye impresiones de la piel.

facts.statement: Barnum Brown describió la especie Chasmosaurus kaiseni en 1933 basándose en el cráneo AMNH 5401, que se distingue por tener cuernos frontales muy largos.
facts.quote: En 1933 Barnum Brown nombró Chasmosaurus kaiseni, en honor a Peter Kaisen y basado en el cráneo AMNH 5401, que difiere de C. belli en tener cuernos muy largos en las cejas.

facts.statement: Richard Swann Lull nombró Chasmosaurus brevirostris en 1933 basándose en el espécimen ROM 839, un cráneo de hocico corto recolectado en 1926.
facts.quote: Richard Swann Lull en 1933 nombró un cráneo inusual, de hocico corto, el espécimen ROM 839 anteriormente ROM 5436 coleccionado en 1926, como Chasmosaurus brevirostris, "con un hocico corto".

facts.statement: Charles Mortram Sternberg describió la especie Chasmosaurus russelli en 1940 basándose en el espécimen NMC 8800 de la formación Dinosaur Park.
facts.quote: Charles Mortram Sternberg agregó Chasmosaurus russelli en 1940, basado en el espécimen NMC 8800 del sudoeste de Alberta parte inferior de la formación Dinosaur Park.

facts.statement: Thomas Lehman describió Chasmosaurus mariscalensis en 1989, aunque esta especie ha sido posteriormente renombrada como Agujaceratops.
facts.quote: Thomas Lehman describió Chasmosaurus mariscalensis en 1989 de Texas, que ahora ha sido renombrado Agujaceratops.

facts.statement: Chasmosaurus irvinensis fue descrita en 2001 a partir de fósiles de las capas superiores de la formación Dinosaur Park.
facts.quote: La especie descrita más recientemente es Chasmosaurus irvinensis nombrada en 2001, que proviene de las capas más altas de la formación Dinosaur Park.

facts.statement: La especie Chasmosaurus irvinensis fue elevada al rango de género independiente, Vagaceratops, en 2010.
facts.quote: Esta especie recibió su propio género, Vagaceratops, en 2010.

facts.statement: Actualmente, solo dos especies de Chasmosaurus se consideran válidas: C. belli y C. russelli.
facts.quote: Hoy, solo dos especies se consideran válidas: C. belli y C. russelli.

facts.statement: Los chasmosaurinos, como Chasmosaurus, poseían hocicos y mandíbulas largos, lo que sugiere que eran más selectivos en su dieta que otros ceratopsianos.
facts.quote: Aparte de la larga gola, los chasmosaurinos tenían un hocico y mandíbulas largos, lo que lleva a sugerir a algunos paleontólogos que eran más selectivos a la hora de comer que sus parientes.

facts.statement: Lawrence Lambe clasificó a Chasmosaurus dentro de la subfamilia Chasmosaurinae en 1915.
facts.quote: Chasmosaurus fue en 1915 incluido por Lambe dentro de la Ceratopsia asignada a los Chasmosaurinae.

facts.statement: La mayoría de los análisis cladísticos sitúan a Chasmosaurus en una posición basal dentro de la subfamilia Chasmosaurinae.
facts.quote: La mayoría de los análisis cladísticos muestran que Chasmosaurus tiene una posición basal en Chasmosaurinae.

facts.statement: El nombre Chasmosaurus proviene del griego y hace referencia a la gran abertura parietal presente en su volante craneal.
facts.quote: Se deriva del griego χάσμα, khasma, "abrir" o "dividir" y se refiere a la fenestra parietal muy grande en el volante del cráneo.

facts.statement: Existe la hipótesis de que Chasmosaurus kaiseni esté relacionado con Chasmosaurus canadensis, aunque esto es debatido.
facts.quote: Esta forma quizás esté relacionada con Chasmosaurus canadensis,'de Canadá', nombrada por Thomas M. Lehman en 1990.

facts.statement: Nicholas Longrich sugirió que Eoceratops y C. kaiseni pertenecían al género Mojoceratops, pero otros estudios indican que Mojoceratops es un sinónimo de Chasmosaurus russelli.
facts.quote: Se pensó que Eoceratops y Chasmosaurus kaiseni de cuernos largos probablemente sean ejemplares de Mojoceratops por Nicholas Longrich, aunque diferentes equipos de investigaciones han encontrado que Mojoceratops es un sinónimo de Chasmosaurus russelli.

facts.statement: Un análisis de 2016 atribuyó a Chasmosaurus indeterminado a Eoceratops y C. kaiseni debido a la ausencia de parietales conservados en sus holotipos.
facts.quote: Campbell y colegas, en su análisis de 2016 de especímenes de Chasmosaurus, encontraron que Eoceratops y C. kaiseni son atribuibles a Chasmosaurus sp. debido a la falta del parietal conservado en los holotipos de ambos.

facts.statement: George Olshevsky propuso en 2000 que Monoclonius recurvicornis fuera Chasmosaurus recurvicornis, aunque esta clasificación es considerada dudosa.
facts.quote: En 2000, George Olshevsky renombró a Monoclonius recurvicornis, Cope 1889, como Chasmosaurus recurvicornis ya que su material fósil es probablemente chasmosaurino. siendo este considerado dudoso.

facts.statement: Fossil evidence from Alberta, Canada, suggests that Chasmosaurus lived in herds.
facts.quote: El hecho de haber encontrado los huesos de varios individuos agrupados en algunos yacimientos en Alberta (Canadá) sugiere que vivían en manadas.

facts.statement: Mass death sites of Chasmosaurus likely formed rapidly due to a catastrophic event, possibly a volcanic eruption.
facts.quote: Los yacimientos de huesos se formaron con gran rapidez debido a algún acontecimiento catastrófico, es posible que por la erupción de un volcán.

facts.statement: Some research suggests a herd of Chasmosaurus died while attempting to swim across a flooded river.
facts.quote: Pero algunas investigaciones han especificado que se trató del desbordamiento de un río, lo que sugiere que toda una manada pereció al intentar cruzar el río a nado.

facts.statement: Researchers hypothesize that male Chasmosaurus could form a defensive ring with frills facing outward against predators like Daspletosaurus.
facts.quote: En caso de los chasmosaurios en una manada que era atacada por a depredador, por ejemplo Daspletosaurus, los machos habría podido formar un anillo y, con todos los volantes haciendo frente hacia fuera, habría presentado una vista formidable.

facts.statement: Chasmosaurus likely had a more selective diet than other ceratopsians due to its longer snout and jaw, suggesting niche partitioning.
facts.quote: El hecho de que Chasmosaurus tenía un hocico y una mandíbula más largas podría haber sido más selectivo con respecto a las plantas que comió lo que sugiere una cierta partición de nicho.

facts.statement: The function of the frill and horns in Chasmosaurus remains a subject of debate.
facts.quote: La función del volante y los cuernos es problemática.

facts.statement: Paul suggested that the beak was the primary defensive weapon for Chasmosaurus.
facts.quote: Paul sugirió que el pico era el arma defensiva principal.

facts.statement: It is possible that the frill of Chasmosaurus was used for intimidation or thermoregulation.
facts.quote: Es posible que el volante se usara simplemente para parecer imponente o para la termorregulación.

facts.statement: The frill of Chasmosaurus may have had bright colors to signal size or for courtship displays.
facts.quote: El volante también puede haber tenido colores brillantes, para llamar la atención sobre su tamaño o como parte de una pantalla de apareamiento.

facts.statement: It is difficult to prove sexual dimorphism in Chasmosaurus based on available evidence.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, es difícil probar cualquier dimorfismo sexual.

facts.statement: A juvenile Chasmosaurus found in Alberta suggests the species may have cared for its young, similar to Triceratops.
facts.quote: Un ejemplar juvenil encontrado en Alberta, Canadá por Phil Currie et al., Revela que Chasmosaurus puede haber cuidado de sus crías, al igual que su pariente, Triceratops que tiene la hipótesis de haberlo hecho.

facts.statement: A juvenile Chasmosaurus specimen measured approximately 1.8 meters in length and was estimated to be three years old.
facts.quote: El juvenil medía alrededor de 1,8 metros de largo y se estimaba que tenía tres años de edad

facts.statement: Evidence suggests Chasmosaurus was not a fast mover, and juveniles did not need to keep up with adults by running quickly.
facts.quote: Esto indica que Chasmosaurus no se movía rápidamente, y que los juveniles no necesitaban moverse rápido para mantener el paso con los adultos.

facts.statement: Matrix evidence indicates the juvenile Chasmosaurus drowned during a possible river crossing.
facts.quote: La evidencia de la matriz en la que fue enterrado indicó que el ceratopsio juvenil se ahogó durante un posible cruce del río.

facts.statement: Studies show juvenile Chasmosaurus had a frill that was narrower on the back and proportionally shorter relative to the skull compared to adults.
facts.quote: Un estudio adicional del espécimen reveló que los chasmosaurs juveniles tenían un volante que era más estrecho en la espalda que el de los adultos, además de ser proporcionalmente más corto en relación con el cráneo.

facts.statement: The genus Chasmosaurus was named by Lambe in 1914.
facts.quote: PBDB name: Chasmosaurus (genus), Lambe 1914

facts.statement: Chasmosaurus belongs to the subfamily Chasmosaurinae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Chasmosaurinae

facts.statement: Chasmosaurus is classified within the family Ceratopsidae.
facts.quote: Family: Ceratopsidae

facts.statement: Chasmosaurus is a member of the class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia

facts.statement: Chasmosaurus lived during the Campanian stage, from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago.
